clue.text: Tease in habitual action? Very sad

indicators.note: one thing placed in another means the tease goes inside the habitual action

blocks.note: a tic is an involuntary habitual twitch or mannerism
to rag someone is to tease them

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether constant teasing is a habit, and finds it all very depressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Habitual action' sounds like a routine; in crosswords it is usually a nervous twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Tragic describes events causing great sorrow or distress, a strong synonym for extremely unhappy.

clue.text: Prohibited cheers with expression of disapproval

blocks.note: ta and cheers are both British informal thanks
booing is a jeer of disapproval

explanation.surface: Drinking toasts are banned, to a chorus of jeers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheers' suggests a toast, but in British speech it also means thank you, as does ta.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taboo is forbidden by custom or social convention, so it is banned from discussion or practice.

clue.text: Mashed potato father had without hesitation

annotation.answer: AT THE DROP OF A HAT

indicators.note: mashing breaks things down and mixes them, so these letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Dad tucked into his mash straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mashed potato' reads as a dish, but mashed is the anagram signal working on potato.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means instantly and readily, as if acting on a signal like a hat dropped to start a race.

clue.text: Lack of movement, batting? Time to wrap it up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means read from the bottom, so the word is backwards
wrapping goes round something, so the time period surrounds the other piece

blocks.note: a batsman in cricket is in while batting
an era is a period of time
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cricket captain urges a stalled batsman that it is time to finish the innings.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the side batting is 'in'. In a down entry, 'up' turns the word it round before the time period wraps it.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is the physical tendency of a body to stay at rest, and figuratively means sluggishness or failure to act.

clue.text: Systems of measurement for plates

blocks.note: first meaning: graded series used for measuring, such as temperature systems
second meaning: the small overlapping plates covering a fish or reptile

explanation.surface: A cook looks for a way to measure portions on dinner plates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plates' suggests crockery, but here it means the hard flakes on a fish's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Celsius and Richter are both graded measuring systems, while a fish's skin is armoured with tiny overlapping flakes.

clue.text: Odd members of clan that spoil a new boat

indicators.note: the odd members are the letters in first, third, fifth positions and so on

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of clan that
to mar is to spoil or damage
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Eccentric members of a family clan wreck a newly built vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clan that' must be read as one string: its odd letters are C, A, T, A.
explanation.definitionFit: A catamaran is a sailing vessel with two parallel hulls, so it is a type of craft that floats.

clue.text: Fruit, large quota distributed

indicators.note: distributing spreads things around, so these letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels
taken as written

explanation.surface: A big allocation of fruit is handed out.
explanation.definitionFit: The loquat is a small yellow plum-like produce from an East Asian evergreen tree, eaten fresh or in jams.

clue.text: Instructions for action in raid get muddled in parts

indicators.note: muddled means confused and jumbled, so the letters come out in a new order
in places the jumbled letters inside the word that follows

blocks.note: taken as written
sections are parts or divisions

explanation.surface: Orders for a military operation become confused in places.
explanation.walkthrough: The scrambled letters sit inside the word for parts, right after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Stage directions are the notes in a script telling actors where to move and what to do, guiding their performance.

clue.text: Speak irritably in card game

blocks.note: first meaning: to say something sharply and crossly
second meaning: a children's game where players call out on matching cards

explanation.surface: A player grumbles crossly during a hand of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: To bark a sharp, short retort is one sense; the other is the simple matching pastime played with a pack.

clue.text: Problem in feline gossip

indicators.note: in sets the problem inside the feline

blocks.note: a cat is a feline
a hitch is a snag or problem

explanation.surface: Neighbours chatter about trouble with a pet cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Chitchat is light, idle conversation about trivial matters, the same informal talk as tittle-tattle.

clue.text: Vegetable, bruised initially, absolute enthusiasts set aside

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word just before it

blocks.note: the first letter of bruised
utter means complete or absolute, as in utter nonsense
a nut is a keen fan, as in a fitness nut
to quash a verdict is to set it aside

explanation.surface: A greengrocer's complaint: the produce was bruised, and the true devotees left it on the shelf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set aside' reads as what the enthusiasts did, but it is the legal sense of annulling a ruling.
explanation.definitionFit: Butternut squash is a pear-shaped, orange-fleshed winter gourd eaten roasted or in soups, so it counts as a vegetable.

clue.text: Roofless old enclosure, architect's last work

indicators.note: last asks for the final letter of the word it is attached to

blocks.note: O is a standard abbreviation for old
a pen is an enclosure for animals
the final letter of architect
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A ruined old building with no roof turns out to be an architect's final commission.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-top bus or car has no roof over its passengers, so it is literally without a covering overhead.

clue.text: Weaving of mat seen to be most skilful

indicators.note: weaving interlaces strands into a new pattern, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Watching a rug being woven shows off the finest craftsmanship.
explanation.walkthrough: MEANEST usually means stingiest; here it is the informal sense of mean as excellent, as in 'plays a mean guitar'.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, mean praises expertise, as in a mean cook, so the superlative describes the greatest expertise.

clue.text: Shabby article about studied obstruction

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the article goes round the rest

blocks.note: the definite article
to read a subject at university is to study it
a bar is a barrier or obstruction

explanation.surface: A worn-out article written on some well-researched blockage.
explanation.walkthrough: Studying a subject at a British university is 'reading' it, so studied is the past tense of read.
explanation.definitionFit: Threadbare clothing is worn so thin the weave shows, giving the shabby look of something long overused.

clue.text: Tedious occasion? Half resolved to disrupt it

indicators.note: half means only part of the word survives, the rest is dropped
disrupting something breaks into it, so one piece is placed inside

blocks.note: a time is an occasion, as in the last time
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dull event, only half sorted out, gets interrupted.
explanation.walkthrough: Keep the first half of RESOLVED, RESO, and break TIME with it: TI(RESO)ME. 'It' refers back to the occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiresome means wearisome or boring, causing fatigue through monotony, which is what tedious describes.

clue.text: Put together plot involving dishonest activity

indicators.note: involving means including within, so the plot surrounds the other piece

blocks.note: a bed is a garden plot for flowers
a racket is a fraudulent scheme

explanation.surface: Conspirators are grouped together for a scheme involving fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' suggests a conspiracy next to dishonest activity; it is a flower bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Bracketed items are grouped or classed alongside one another, as if enclosed within the same pair of brackets.

clue.text: Eccentric hobby to some extent ridiculous

indicators.note: to some extent means only partly, so just a portion of the phrase is used

blocks.note: found inside eccentRIC Hobby

explanation.surface: Someone finds a strange pastime somewhat laughable.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'that's rich' scoffs at something absurd or preposterous, especially hypocrisy, so the word can mean laughable.

clue.text: Run, fit and ecstatic

blocks.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
apt means fitting or suitable

explanation.surface: A jogger out running feels healthy and elated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fit' pairs naturally with running as healthy; here it means suitable.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapt describes someone carried away with delight or completely absorbed, which overlaps with being joyfully transported.

clue.text: Most unusual to store data in tropical environment

indicators.note: storing something means keeping it inside, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: rare means unusual, so this is the superlative
info is short for information, or data

explanation.surface: Researchers find it highly unusual to keep their records out in the jungle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most unusual' looks like a description of storing data, but it is a superlative that holds the data inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rainforest is dense, wet woodland typical of hot equatorial regions, a habitat found in the tropics.

clue.text: Covering part of disloyal revolution up

indicators.note: part of means only a section of the following words is used
in a down entry, up means the letters run from bottom to top

blocks.note: found inside disloYAL REVOlution

explanation.surface: Part of a treacherous uprising is concealed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolution' hints at turning round, but it only supplies letters; up is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An overlay is a layer laid on top of something else, such as a transparent sheet or veneer, so it is a coating.

clue.text: Teacher put away present

blocks.note: a don is a university lecturer
to put away food is to eat it

explanation.surface: A tutor tidies away a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a noun for a gift; it is the verb meaning to give.
explanation.definitionFit: To donate is to give money or goods as a gift, which is one sense of the verb present.

clue.text: Be morose, keeping away after retirement in county

indicators.note: keeping means holding within, so the sulking word surrounds the other piece
retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: to sulk is to be sullen and morose
off means away, as in going off

explanation.surface: A grumpy pensioner keeps to themselves after retiring to the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: SUFFOLK is a county on the east coast of England. SULK holds OFF reversed: SU(FFO)LK.
explanation.definitionFit: Suffolk is one of the administrative shires of East Anglia, and county is the British term for such a region.

clue.text: Robbed, cold and angry

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
a heated person is worked up or angry

explanation.surface: A burglary victim is left chilled and furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold and angry' sound like contrasting temperatures; cold is just the tap letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To be cheated is to be swindled or deprived of something by deception, close in meaning to being stolen from.

clue.text: Extract fastener

blocks.note: first meaning: a short excerpt from a film or programme
second meaning: a device such as a paper or hair grip

explanation.definitionFit: A film excerpt shown on television is a short snippet, and a paperclip or hairgrip holds things together.

clue.text: Study one beginning to mend fabric

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: a den is a private room for study
I is the Roman numeral one
the first letter of mend

explanation.surface: A student sets about repairing some cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Study' looks like a verb but is the room.
explanation.definitionFit: Denim is a sturdy twilled cotton cloth used for jeans, so it is a type of textile.

clue.text: Love song, terrible trial when gloomy

indicators.note: something terrible is in a bad state, so the following words get mangled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A romantic ballad becomes an ordeal when you are feeling down.
explanation.walkthrough: MY HEART WILL GO ON is Celine Dion's 1997 theme from the film Titanic.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titanic theme is a romantic ballad about enduring devotion, so it is a classic example of a romantic number.

clue.text: Cool and objective in test

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other, here the objective inside the test

blocks.note: a try is an attempt or test
an end is an aim or objective

explanation.surface: An examiner is calm and impartial during an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cool and objective' reads as a calm, fair person; cool is the slang definition and objective a noun meaning aim. TR(END)Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Trendy means fashionable and up to date, which is what cool means in its informal slang sense.

clue.text: Sticky substance covering spot around mineral

indicators.note: covering means wrapping round, so the sticky substance goes outside
turned around means facing the other way, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: gum is a sticky adhesive
to spot something is to spy it

explanation.surface: Some glue has been smeared round a blemish on a rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spot' looks like a noun for a mark; it is the verb meaning catch sight of. G(YPS)UM.
explanation.definitionFit: Gypsum is a soft calcium sulphate rock used to make plaster, a naturally occurring crystalline compound.
